fields.summary: The shipit work plan for task 5: a derived SQLite index per worktree, caught up from the log by reading only new entry files, holding the as-is and to-be views, plus a deterministic 50,000-node generator and a read budget test. Decided (D1-D15, agent wording accepted by the owner): a new internal/index package with no command wired and the api's interim model untouched; the pure-Go modernc.org/sqlite driver, so no cgo; the index lives in the user cache folder keyed by a hash of the worktree root; input-incremental catch-up that decodes only new entries, refolds touched change sets and recomputes a view whole when its inputs change, writing rows by diff; as-is and to-be are stored and what-if is computed on demand and benchmarked; freshness is judged by entry file names, and any vanished file forces a full rebuild; the generator is a Go package, deterministic from a seed, with a realistic mix of about 35,000 nodes and 15,000 links over about 500 change sets; a budget test in make check plus benchmarks; a schema version, rebuild on mismatch or corruption, and catch-up under an immediate transaction with WAL and a busy timeout; a minimal per-view query API; tests after implementation, including a property that any split into catch-up steps equals a scratch build; the fresh-read median must stay under 25 ms over 20 runs; no ADR. Revised after the plan: the orchestrator later raised the fresh-read budget to 50 ms, milestone 1's target, after CI on main failed at 27.4 ms (PR #11). Left open: a faster fresh read so CI has headroom under 25 ms again.
fields.title: Shipit plan, milestone 1 task 5: the SQLite index
